transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Dr. Elaine Park (Vantage CISO), Tom Reyes (Head of Infra), Priya Bose (Security Eng), Sahil Mehta (DevOps)
Link to artifacts: redwood deck (https://redwood.example/decks/vmed-security), pen-test export (shared link, redacted): https://files.redwood.example/vmed/pentest-redacted-2026-02

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Quick readout of external engagement with third-party red-team (scope: hosted API + VPC connectors).
- Top findings: two critical remote code exec vectors in older python dependencies in sidecar, several medium auth misconfigurations (RBAC rules too permissive), audit log gaps for cross-region failover events.
- Discussed remediation options (patch cadence, canary deploys, backport support), KMS integration options for BYOK, and next steps around ownership mapping and follow-up tests.

Transcript:
00:00 Maya: okay uh good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account.
00:08 Dr. Park: hey thanks Maya, Elaine here, appreciate you making time.
00:12 Carlos: hi all, Carlos from Redwood infra, i'll be going over the tech readout and some of our logs and suggested tests.
00:20 Tom: tom here, sorry for being a minute late traffic.. um let's get into it.
00:30 Maya: quick agenda, high level pen test readout, vuln triage, patch cadence discussion, KMS/encryption options, and then Q&A and next steps.
00:45 Maya: quick note, the pen-test report is redacted to remove customer PII, link in the deck.
01:05 Carlos: okay starting with the external findings, the red team ran a mixed black/white box on the hosted endpoints plus the VPC peering connector. primary critical finding was a remote code path in an older sidecar dependency - python wheel, i think they referenced CVE-2024-XXXX. transcription note: they spelled it CVE- two zero four four X X X X in the report, but it's the one we've seen in other scans.
01:40 Dr. Park: can you clarify sidecar — is that our proxy sidecar on the dedicated hosts, or the customer side?
01:46 Carlos: uh yeah, so it's the connector sidecar that runs in the customer's k8s (kube) nodes that talk to Redwood's VPC tunnel. in some of their staging clusters an old package slipped in.
02:05 Priya: that matches what our scan saw, we had a couple of images with outdated deps in canary namespace.
02:15 Maya: ok -- so immediate mitigation question, is this patchable without downtime?
02:20 Carlos: short answer - yes, with a rolling canary patch and circuit-breaker on the sidecar we can update. risk is if we do full cluster restart you'll bump active sessions so we recommend canary then traffic-shift.
02:40 Tom: what's the suggested rollback window? we generally target 15 minutes for canary observation.
02:45 Carlos: 15-30 minutes is our baseline; but for security patches we usually wait for 60m health metrics to be safe if it touches cache invalidation.
03:10 Dr. Park: audit logs — the test showed gaps when the vpc failover triggered across regions, can you expand?
03:20 Carlos: yeah so the red team simulated region failover; the audit stream pipeline (our lambda/forwarder) dropped a subset of events during the DNS re-resolve in one of their envs. basically, retention was fine but there was a ~45s window where certain request headers weren't captured.
03:45 Priya: we saw similar — our internal app logs show the event but the centralized audit index missed the headers. possible race in the forwarder on reconnect.
04:05 Maya: any compliance implications for SOC2 or ISO?
04:10 Carlos: for SOC2 it flags as a control gap in change monitoring / logging completeness; not necessarily evidence of breach but you want to remediate and add compensating controls like buffering and local durable queue on the forwarder so no telemetry drops.
04:30 Dr. Park: KMS question — we want BYOK, HSM-backed keys, and per-tenant key separation. how far along is Redwood on that?
04:40 Carlos: we support multiple KMS integrations already, we have a BYOK workflow in Private deployments and Dedicated. Hosted API currently supports customer-managed keys via partner KMS with per-tenant envelope encryption, but i'll be candid — there are some work items for fully rolling the HSM-backed per-tenant key lifecycle across all regions.
05:05 Tom: and any FIPS or HSM certs required for us? we need FIPS-140-2 on some workloads.
05:10 Carlos: we have FIPS-enabled modules in our enterprise package for Private, we can discuss certs with our compliance team; i'll include the compliance whitepaper.
05:30 Maya: okay let's go into vuln triage. who owns the different classes?
05:35 Priya: generally our org wants vendor-to-customer mapping: Redwood owns runtime and infra components in hosted mode; customer owns sidecar and any connectors you run in your cluster. but we can extend support for patch backports on Dedicated under contract.
05:55 Dr. Park: so the connector sidecar is our responsibility — is that documented?
06:00 Maya: yes it's in the integration guide, albeit the naming there sometimes says "connector agent" which caused some confusion.
06:15 Priya: small note — the report had a mislabel, they called our KV cache "K V cache" in one section, might confuse legal.
06:25 Carlos: haha yeah the speech-to-text of the tool did that.
06:35 Tom: ok remediation prioritization, what are the top 3 we need to address in 30 days?
06:40 Carlos: 1) patch sidecar python deps (critical RCE), 2) enforce stricter RBAC on cluster roles for the connector (medium), 3) add buffering to audit forwarder and increase retention of raw request logs by 30 days (low/medium).
07:05 Dr. Park: patch cadence - our board wants monthly security patch cycles for infra libs and quarterly for feature stacks, can Redwood support that?
07:15 Maya: we can support a monthly patch cadence for connector images, with a recommended emergency patch path for critical CVEs. for hosted runtime we do scheduled maintenance windows monthly but major model infra backports are on a quarterly track unless critical.
07:35 Sahil: do you provide CVE alerts via slack or our ticketing system?
07:40 Carlos: yes, we can push to your Jira project and send slack alerts to the security channel. we'll include the CVE number, exploitability, and mitigation steps.
07:55 Dr. Park: remediation SLAs? what about penalties or credits?
08:00 Maya: contractual SLAs for Dedicated/Private can be tailored; for Hosted we provide RTO-ish timelines and prioritization but not financial credits by default. enterprise deals can include stricter terms.
08:20 Tom: can you walk us through the KMS flow for BYOK quickly?
08:25 Carlos: sure - in our Dedicated/Private flow we support key import to an HSM or a cloud-KMS; we use envelope encryption - data keys are generated per-tenant and encrypted with the customer's master key. Redwood never stores the plaintext master key. in hosted we have a partner KMS flow where customer provides a key resource in their cloud account and we perform secure calls.
08:55 Priya: will that have audit trail for key ops? we need key rotation logs and who invoked decrypt.
09:00 Carlos: yes we emit key operation events to the audit pipeline with key-id, operation, and calling principal. retention depends on your compliance package.
09:20 Dr. Park: data residency — we need logs to stay in EU for EU patients, can you ensure region-locate logs and keys?
09:26 Maya: region pinning is supported for Private and Dedicated, hosted we can region-route on request for enterprise customers, but there are caveats with multi-region failover which we discussed earlier.
09:50 Carlos: if you need strict residency we'll recommend Dedicated in EU with KMS in your account and block cross-region replication for those datasets.
10:12 Tom: alright let's talk about secure SDLC changes - what does Redwood expect from us in terms of git signing or attestations?
10:20 Priya: we saw a note in the report about unsigned images in the canary namespace. we want to start requiring image signing and attestations in our CI.
10:28 Maya: Redwood supports image verification via in-cluster admission controllers and can verify signatures on connector images. we have a doc for image attestation integration.
10:40 Sahil: what's the recommended rollback policy if we detect a signature mismatch in prod?
10:45 Carlos: fail closed; block deployment and send an alert. for running instances we recommend an emergency canary rollback if you suspect compromise.
11:00 Dr. Park: how real is the exploit? was it low complexity?
11:05 Carlos: red-team assessed as high likelihood if not patched, they had a working PoC in staging. exploit complexity was moderate - required an unpatched dependency plus malformed payload.
11:25 Priya: do you have recommended patching windows for our 3-week sprint cadence? we usually prefer not to break sprints.
11:32 Maya: recommended - schedule security patch merges in a dedicated weekly window or cherry-pick into release branches; emergency patches can be hot-fixed outside the cadence.
11:50 Tom: logging — do you recommend an increase in retention for raw HTTP request logs? we currently do 90 days.
11:58 Carlos: for compliance you may want 180 days for critical audit streams; at least archive compressed raw logs after 90 days into cold storage with integrity checks.
12:20 Dr. Park: can Redwood redact PHI from logs automatically? our concern is inadvertent patient data in request payloads.
12:28 Carlos: we have PII/PHI masking rules for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private you can configure regex-based masks in the forwarder. we should run a PII audit on the sample logs.
12:45 Priya: note — the report referenced an old SAML 2.0 assertion flow, said a misconfigured ACS URL could allow assertion reuse. do you have mitigations?
12:55 Carlos: re: SAML — ensure strict audience and recipient checks, enforce One-time use of assertions if possible, and add assertion replay detection in the IDP.
13:10 Dr. Park: our compliance officer will want to see traceability for all admin actions - do you provide immutable admin audit logs?
13:18 Maya: yes we provide admin action logs with write-once retention for Private; for Hosted we provide audit events with append-only storage, and we can offer journaled export to your SIEM.
13:35 Tom: about the red team's medium finding - overly permissive RBAC, how granular can we get in role definitions for the connector?
13:42 Carlos: the connector uses a small set of roles; we can make them more granular — e.g., separate read-only telemetry extraction from config write rights. that's a config change in the helm chart.
14:05 Priya: any automation for scanning images for known vulns on push? we want gate in CI.
14:12 Carlos: yes we support registry scans and webhooks; Redwood can fail CI if a critical CVE is found above threshold. we can share a sample pipeline.
14:35 Dr. Park: do you track RCE severity differently to auth bypass or info leak? we want prioritization scoring.
14:43 Maya: we use CVSS + exploitability + customer-specific impact to drive prioritization. we'll surface a triage score in the tracker.
15:00 Sahil: the red-team also mentioned a timing window on the KV cache that could be used to exfiltrate keys - is that accurate?
15:08 Carlos: yes they had a side channel that could leak small amounts in a noisy scenario; mitigation is to reduce the cache TTL for sensitive keys and add constant-time operations for key comparisons. we'd also rotate data keys and monitor for abnormal access patterns.
15:35 Dr. Park: rotation cadence? quarterly? monthly?
15:40 Carlos: we recommend quarterly rotation for data keys by default; for high-risk tenants monthly. Master's rotation is more careful and tied to operational windows.
15:55 Maya: i want to call out some of the ambiguities in the report — there were a few false positives and a couple of mis-named components. we'll clarify these in the redacted deliverable.
16:10 Priya: okay for ownership mapping - can we put owners in a spreadsheet and have Redwood mark which ones you're willing to patch vs customer-owned?
16:18 Maya: yes we'll provide a remediation tracker with columns: finding, owner (Redwood/Customer/Hybrid), mitigation steps, target date, verification steps.
16:30 Dr. Park: verification steps - do you do rescans or we'll run canary exploit attempts?
16:36 Carlos: we can do both — Redwood can run a targeted verification scan and we recommend customer run a small canary exploit test in a staging environment.
16:55 Tom: on the CVE backlog, do you offer backporting for older runtime versions? we run some pinned versions for stability.
17:02 Carlos: we do backport support as a paid professional service for Dedicated customers; for Hosted we recommend moving to supported runtime versions but we can coordinate patch backports in urgent cases.
17:25 Dr. Park: legal will ask about evidence for SOC2 controls - can you provide change history and proof of remediation?
17:30 Maya: yes — we can provide remediation artifacts, PRs, releases, and audit trails tied to the remediation ticket. we'll attach those to attestation evidence.
17:50 Priya: do you support SSO groups with SCIM provisioning? we want automated RBAC group sync.
17:55 Carlos: yes we support SCIM for group sync; mapping rules exist in the console for RBAC role assignment.
18:10 Dr. Park: okay can you summarize the critical exposure and our immediate actions?
18:15 Carlos: critical exposure: patch sidecar RCE (urgent), tighten RBAC on connector roles, add buffer to audit forwarder. immediate actions: patch canary, increase log retention for 30 days, map owners.
18:40 Maya: next steps recap - we'll -> send redacted report + remediation tracker by 2/23; Carlos will run the KV cache ingress test and share logs by 2/28; customer to assign owners by 2/27; schedule KMS walkthrough week of 3/2.
19:05 Dr. Park: and we will want a canary exploit re-test, ideally in our staging.
19:12 Carlos: yes we'll coordinate that.
19:20 Sahil: quick Q on implementation detail — does the BYOK flow require an open firewall rule from our KMS to Redwood?
19:27 Carlos: no, for partner KMS flows we use an egress-only encrypted connection; keys are not exposed and calls are outbound from Redwood into your KMS via secure channels. we'll share network diagram.
19:45 Tom: any follow-up on the audit pipeline fix timeline?
19:50 Carlos: we'll propose a patch for the forwarder buffer in the remediation tracker, target is 2-week turnaround after acceptance.
20:05 Maya: ok great, thanks everyone. any final Qs?
20:10 Dr. Park: nothing else from me, appreciate the thoroughness.
20:15 Priya: thanks all.
20:20 Maya: end notes - i'll email the docs and tracker. meeting adjourned.

Post-call notes (auto):
- We noted a few transcription glitches in the red-team report names (CVE ids, component names); Redwood will ensure precise naming in the shared artifacts.
- Customer requested BYOK HSM details and FIPS evidence; Redwood to attach compliance whitepaper.
- Action items assigned (see above).

End of transcript.
